diagnoses.lesson: Translate each contract into shared, ordered validation and state-transition rules; test boundary cases and cross-chunk behavior before optimizing.
Parse and validate the entire input before applying changes; keep coordinates, counts, and ordering explicit, and rank every valid match by the specified rules.

diagnoses.bug: The requirements create tricky precedence and boundary cases: syntax errors must be found before value processing, nested braces outrank content validation, and percent triplets are greedily preserved while malformed percent signs are encoded.
diagnoses.lesson: Separate parsing, validation, and expansion; track UTF-8 byte offsets explicitly, define error precedence, and test boundary cases before processing values.
Validate encodings in a deliberate order: integrity and canonical form first, then structure and bounds, while preserving container boundaries in recursive parsing.
Translate requirements into explicit parsing, validation, and evaluation phases; preserve error precedence and test boundary cases across each phase.
When implementing a parser, enforce validation stages in the specified order and track byte offsets through every transformation.
Translate dense requirements into explicit invariants and precedence rules before coding; preserve distinctions that affect equality or boundary behavior.
Translate detailed requirements into explicit invariants and operation order; preserve specified intermediate failures, error precedence, and edge cases.
Validate inputs in explicit precedence order, then separate parsing from layout; track original offsets and model line state explicitly.

diagnoses.bug: The requirements combine exact parsing precedence, partial-range expansion, prerelease admission, discrete SemVer intersection, and canonicalization; treating version ranges as ordinary numeric intervals misses identifier-level adjacency and finite-boundary cases.
diagnoses.lesson: Model parsers as ordered state machines, and model precedence domains with their true discrete structure; test boundary and error-order cases before simplifying.
Translate each rule into an explicit invariant, then test precedence, boundary cases, and shared behavior across all public operations.
Translate the full specification into explicit validation, search, and error-precedence rules before coding; recompute branch-local derived state after every assignment.
Separate raw-input validation from traversal, preserve original byte offsets through every transformation, and test precedence and boundary cases explicitly.
Translate requirements into an explicit validation order and atomic state transitions; test boundary cases and verify every observable output, including logs and counters.
Validate inputs in the specified precedence before transforming data; then preserve token boundaries and apply layout using the stated measurement units.
Validate inputs in their specified order, then process the logical data as one stream; preserve state across chunks and boundaries, and test edge cases explicitly.
Validate operations before mutating state, and define ordering and arithmetic explicitly so ties, errors, and extreme values behave deterministically.
Define cursor validation, failure precedence, and per-item error origins explicitly; check bounds before reading, then test boundary cases and full-width values.

diagnoses.bug: The requirements impose a strict validation order and a deterministic rightmost tie-break during width reduction; implementing these as incidental checks or unstable iteration can return the wrong error or allocate widths incorrectly.
diagnoses.lesson: Make precedence explicit: validate in ordered passes, then apply deterministic tie-breaks, and preserve Unicode scalar boundaries throughout transformation.
Track parser state and byte offsets explicitly; apply validation in the specified order, and test chunk boundaries, EOF, and error precedence.
Translate each stated validation pass into an explicit ordered phase, preserving input indices and deferring later work until the entire required pass succeeds.

lessons: Translate requirements into explicit ordered validation, parsing, and state-transition phases; define error precedence, invariants, and boundary cases before choosing an algorithm.
Validate all required input before mutation or output; preserve original indices, offsets, metadata, and distinctions that affect equality or errors.
Track positions and state explicitly across transformations, chunks, and boundaries; preserve source offsets, token boundaries, and UTF-8 scalar boundaries.
Model operations as ordered phases, applying admission, expiry, validation, and mutation exactly when specified; commit only completed work and preserve failed items.
Use checked arithmetic at each required operation or prefix; define bounds, rounding stages, and overflow precedence explicitly.
Use complete comparators and explicit tie-breaks; never rely on incidental container order.
Separate scanning and parsing from output construction; track source and transformed positions independently, and emit only after required validation succeeds.
Verify every observable result, including logs and counters, and test shared behavior, error precedence, and boundary cases across public operations.
previous_lessons: Translate requirements into explicit validation order, output invariants, stable ordering, and edge cases before choosing an algorithm.
Validate inputs and preflight failure conditions before mutation; preserve original indices, offsets, metadata, and optional-value distinctions explicitly.
Model operations as ordered phases, applying admission, expiry, validation, and mutation exactly when specified.
Use checked arithmetic at each required operation or prefix, and define bounds, rounding stages, and overflow precedence explicitly.
Separate scanning and parsing phases from output construction; track source positions and transformed output positions independently.
Track streaming state and physical input offsets across chunks; emit results only after the required validation succeeds.
Keep each ordering structure aligned with its contract, using complete comparators instead of incidental container order.
Preserve failed items and commit only completed work; represent scoped data, snapshots, and deadlines independently.
